dedupe_keys.name: hapi heliophysics data api specification and client libraries

description: HAPI, the Heliophysics Data Application Programmer's Interface, is a specification for downloading and streaming time series, with client libraries in Python (hapiclient), IDL, Javascript, Julia and MATLAB and a list of compliant servers. It was developed by the heliophysics community and was recommended by COSPAR in 2018 as the common data access API for space science and space weather data, so that users can load data into an array with one command instead of writing file readers. Coverage is whatever the HAPI servers publish, which includes NASA CDAWeb and other space weather archives worldwide, at their native cadence. Format and access: REST requests returning CSV, JSON or binary; a web interface generates download scripts and preview plots; the Python client was at version 0.3.3 in August 2026. Licence: not stated as an SPDX licence on the pages read; use is free. Caveats: data quality and licences belong to each server, and not every archive is HAPI-compliant. It prepares solar wind, magnetometer and particle time series for space weather hazard exposure studies and operational digital twins. Related catalogue records are NASA OMNIWeb and SuperMAG, typical space weather sources reached through such interfaces.
